findings.message: The graph grounding is hollow for this Story's new files. Every changed symbol except resolveCompanionHeader has an empty testsReaching list, even where a dedicated test file exists that drives the symbol (panzoom.test.ts calls insrcPanZoom.init, completeness.test.ts calls completenessFindings, plus er-page, sequence-component-page, ux-page, shell, header, companion-context-finalize, diagram-handlers and ux dimension tests). No not-exercised HIGHs were raised from the empty edges. Instead, coverage was judged by running the suites: companion + finalize + code-review subsets ran 369 tests, 367 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (the Chrome live smoke and a pre-existing grounding IPC live test). Every other promised test maps to a present, passing test file. 'tsc --noEmit' and the docgen pipeline tests were not re-run in this review.
findings.expectationRef: testsReaching grounding (indexer edge gap on new files)

findings.message: The same one-line HIGH-breach DimensionFinding factory is copied into component.ts, er.ts:183, sequence.ts:166, ux.ts:189 and code-review/dimensions/ux/index.ts:82. Only the DIMENSION constant differs between the copies. One shared helper, breach(dimension, location, message), would stop the severity and confidence shape from drifting between modules. Each copy is trivial, so this is not a real risk.

shortText (cuts at 60 characters, collapses whitespace) and truncate at ux.ts:230 (cuts at 40, keeps whitespace as is) are two ellipsis truncators in the same module. Their limits and whitespace handling differ, so one label can render differently in the Elements section and in the key-element table. One parameterised helper would be clearer. This is a matter of taste.
